title: Dispense a two-thirds cup of slush and set it on the pickup stand
instruction: Pick up the plastic cup, place it on the drip tray under the slushie tap, pull the tap handle to fill it about two-thirds, then put the filled cup on the serving stand.
context: At a concession counter, a worker meters each serving by releasing the tap as the drink reaches the requested level. The worker then carries the open cup from the drip tray to the pickup stand. Portion size and spilled volume can both be measured at handoff.
setup: On a fixed two-arm YAM station, x points forward, y points left, and the tabletop is at z = 0.7475 m. An empty, upright PET cup starts on the brushed-steel pickup stand with its base at (0.300, 0.200, 0.888) m. The tapered cup is 110 mm tall, 58 mm across at the base and 93 mm at the rim, with a 0.6 mm wall, 12 g empty mass and 479 mL capacity. The stand has a 130 mm square base, a 122 mm pedestal and a 72 mm round platform at z = 0.8875 m. The machine has a 360 × 340 × 250.5 mm steel cabinet, a clear acrylic bowl 300 mm long and 210 mm in diameter, and a 125 mm spring-return lever. The tap starts closed at −15°. Its outlet is at (0.385, 0, 0.995) m, above a 125 × 170 × 16 mm steel drip tray with its top at z = 0.860 m. Physical reference: VEVOR R1-RXR02(W)-N7-3-01 (US listing $162.99), or the approximately $95–125 gravity fixture in physical-trial.md. Use 210 g sucrose and 1,290 g water per batch (14% by mass). For the gravity fixture, chill to 2–4 °C and freeze with mixing to fine crystals. For the VEVOR machine, start with liquid at 20 ± 5 °C and use its slush program. Serve at −1.7 to −1.2 °C. Qualify the physical rig with a 125 mm return lever, 135 mm spout-to-tray clearance (25 mm above cup rim) and a target full-open flow of 60 mL/s (acceptable measured range 54–66 mL/s). The protocol includes the intermediate flow checks. A simulated bench scale uses the pickup stand as its pan. A digital temperature probe sits in the hopper. equipment-reproduction.md gives sourced parts, linkage dimensions and the mapping from the fixture to the simulated interfaces.
scoring: Four milestones accumulate up to 0.60 points. Lifting the cup base more than 8 mm above the pickup platform earns 0.10. Bringing it within 15 mm horizontally and 6 mm vertically of the target under the spout earns 0.15. Opening the tap beyond 30% earns 0.10. Peak volume collected earns up to 0.25, increasing linearly to 60% of cup capacity. Once the cup has held 60–73% of capacity, each of six current conditions earns one sixth of the remaining 0.40 points. (1) cup base within 15 mm horizontally and 4 mm vertically of its pickup position, (2) tilt below 5°, (3) fill within 60–73% inclusive, (4) less than 5% of dispensed volume spilled, (5) both hands at least 5 mm clear of the cup, with cup speed below 10 mm/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s, and (6) tap within 5° of closed. The three manipulation milestones must have occurred and all six final conditions must hold for one continuous second to end the trial successfully. At timeout, the final step determines the score. In physical trials weigh source loss and net cup contents. Separately weigh all spill, including retained drips on the tray and grate, pad covers, pan and wipes. Convert mass to bulk-equivalent mL with measured batch density. Include delayed drips in the five-second collection window. Check mass closure and apply the same strict 5% spill limit (physical-trial.md).
fidelity: Cup and tap motion follow rigid-body contact. The measured lever angle sets flow up to 60 mL/s. Falling portions enter through the cup rim. Retained volume sets the horizontal surface height in the tapered cup, and liquid above the lowest rim spills. The model tracks 900 mL of available slush. It omits transient sloshing, individual ice crystals and puddle motion. The hopper display stays fixed. Instrument panels display simulated gross cup mass at the pickup stand and hopper temperature. The scale assumes a bulk density of 1.05 g/mL. The probe follows a lumped refrigerated-batch model. Independent load-cell forces are outside the model. Simulated slush increases the rigid cup mass while its inertia tensor stays fixed. Preparation uses an ideal-solution ice fraction and assumed cooling power. An assumed nozzle hold-up produces post-closure drips. Thin tip covers change contact friction and a secondary pan catches projected overflow.
scores: Simulation (seed 0): scripted demo 1.00 in 1,539 control steps (76.95 s); Dream-1 0.10 in 2,400 control steps (120 s).
reset_notes: Protect both grippers with fitted pad covers and the carry path with a catch pan. After each trial, weigh the collectors, clean and dry pads, tray and stand, and replace the empty cup. Reset the closed tap and starting inventory. Verify batch temperature, density and flow, restore inventory after test draws, then tare again.
